text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Kimi announced research grants of up to $20,000 in API credits for selected science and engineering teams, with first-round applications due December 8. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6764)

2 — tinygrad announced a free inference trial offering Qwen 3.8 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash with 262k context, up to five concurrent connections and GitHub signup. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6765)

3 — Citing Reuters, kimmonismus reports that hackers exploited a software flaw to breach the US Air Force's Cloud One control plane, with Cyber Command assessing the damage. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6766)

4 — techartist_ says they used Gemini 4 Neon to turn an evolution chapter into an interactive field journal with 10 hands-on lessons, museum and field measurements, and a visual test. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6767)

5 — Liquid AI released d1.3-ultra, claiming first place on Artificial Analysis's decision index 2.1 and improved policy-following, ranking, image/audio extraction and audio time-span identification. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6768)

6 — kimmonismus quotes Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark saying the singularity has begun and describes his fiction about humans needing a new discipline to interpret AI discoveries. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6769)

7 — alexmichael shared a post noting that someone had made a bingo card for the remainder of the year. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6770)

8 — François Chollet rejected claims that 2026's mathematical progress exceeds the preceding 140 years, arguing that mathematical understanding remains nearly unchanged from 2025. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6771)

9 — Markov Robotics introduced X-Ray, claiming it converts monocular first-person video into millimeter-accurate 3D poses with jitter-free tracking even under full occlusion. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6772)

--Hermes
